description: A type of vaginal inflammation caused by the overgrowth of bacteria naturally found in the vagina, which upsets the natural balance.
causes: Overgrowth of certain bacteria, often linked to new or multiple sex partners or douching.
symptoms: Thin, gray, white or green vaginal discharge
prevention: Avoid douching, limit sex partners, and use mild, non-scented soaps.
treatment_action: Prescription antibiotics (pills or creams).
complications: Increased risk of STIs and preterm birth.
medical_disclaimer: This information is for educational purposes only and is not a substitute for professional medical advice.

description: Inflammation of the head of the penis (the glans).
causes: Poor hygiene, infections (yeast or bacteria), or skin conditions.
prevention: Good hygiene, especially for uncircumcised men.
treatment_action: Antifungal or antibiotic creams, and improved hygiene.
complications: Phimosis (inability to retract foreskin) and scarring.
medical_disclaimer: This information is for educational purposes only and is not a substitute for professional medical advice.

description: A condition in which the lining of the esophagus is damaged by stomach acid and changed to a lining similar to that of the small intestine.
causes: Long-term gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD).
prevention: Treating GERD symptoms early and effectively.
treatment_action: Monitoring with endoscopy, and sometimes surgery or ablation.
complications: Increased risk of esophageal cancer.
medical_disclaimer: This information is for educational purposes only and is not a substitute for professional medical advice.

description: A fluid-filled swelling in the Bartholin's glands, which are located on each side of the vaginal opening.
causes: Blockage of the gland's duct.
symptoms: Painless lump near the vaginal opening
prevention: Safe sex and good hygiene may help prevent infection of a cyst.
treatment_action: Sitz baths, drainage, or antibiotics if infected.
complications: Abscess formation.
medical_disclaimer: This information is for educational purposes only and is not a substitute for professional medical advice.

description: A type of skin cancer that begins in the basal cells.
causes: Long-term exposure to ultraviolet (UV) radiation from sunlight.
symptoms: A flat, flesh-colored or brown scar-like lesion
A bleeding or scabbing sore that heals and returns
prevention: Avoid peak sun, use sunscreen, and wear protective clothing.
treatment_action: Surgical excision, Mohs surgery, or radiation therapy.
complications: Recurrence and spread to surrounding tissues.
medical_disclaimer: This information is for educational purposes only and is not a substitute for professional medical advice.

description: A condition that causes sudden, temporary weakness in the facial muscles.
causes: Likely caused by viral infections that lead to swelling of the facial nerve.
symptoms: Rapid onset of mild weakness to total paralysis on one side of the face
Facial droop and difficulty making facial expressions
Pain around the jaw or behind the ear
prevention: No known way to prevent Bell's palsy.
treatment_action: Corticosteroids and antiviral drugs.
complications: Irreversible damage to the facial nerve and eye problems.
medical_disclaimer: This information is for educational purposes only and is not a substitute for professional medical advice.

description: A condition in men in which the prostate gland is enlarged and not cancerous.
causes: Changes in hormone balance as men get older.
symptoms: Frequent or urgent need to urinate
Increased frequency of urination at night
prevention: No known way to prevent, but a healthy diet and exercise may help.
treatment_action: Medications, minimally invasive procedures, or surgery.
complications: Urinary tract infections, bladder stones, and kidney damage.
medical_disclaimer: This information is for educational purposes only and is not a substitute for professional medical advice.

description: A mental health condition that causes extreme mood swings that include emotional highs (mania or hypomania) and lows (depression).
causes: Biological differences and genetics.
prevention: No known way to prevent, but early treatment can help prevent worsening.
treatment_action: Medications (mood stabilizers) and psychotherapy.
complications: Problems related to drug and alcohol use, suicide or suicide attempts.
medical_disclaimer: This information is for educational purposes only and is not a substitute for professional medical advice.

description: A type of cancer that begins in the cells of the bladder.
causes: Smoking, chemical exposure, and chronic bladder inflammation.
prevention: Don't smoke, take caution with chemicals, and drink plenty of water.
treatment_action: Surgery, chemotherapy, radiation therapy, or immunotherapy.
complications: Recurrence and spread to other organs.
medical_disclaimer: This information is for educational purposes only and is not a substitute for professional medical advice.

description: An infection caused by breathing in the fungus Blastomyces dermatitidis.
causes: Exposure to moist soil and decomposing matter containing the fungus.
prevention: Avoid areas where the fungus is known to live, especially if immunocompromised.
treatment_action: Antifungal medications.
complications: Spread to skin, bones, and central nervous system.
medical_disclaimer: This information is for educational purposes only and is not a substitute for professional medical advice.

description: A blood clot that forms in a vein deep in the body, usually in the lower leg or thigh.
causes: Injury to a vein, surgery, certain medications, and limited movement.
symptoms: Red or discolored skin on the leg
A feeling of warmth in the affected leg
prevention: Avoid sitting still for long periods, exercise regularly, and manage weight.
treatment_action: Blood thinners (anticoagulants) and compression stockings.
complications: Pulmonary embolism (clot travels to lungs).
medical_disclaimer: This information is for educational purposes only and is not a substitute for professional medical advice.

description: A rare cancer that forms in a bone.
causes: Genetic syndromes and radiation exposure.
symptoms: Swelling and tenderness near the affected area
prevention: No known way to prevent bone cancer.
treatment_action: Surgery, chemotherapy, and radiation therapy.
complications: Spread to other parts of the body.
medical_disclaimer: This information is for educational purposes only and is not a substitute for professional medical advice.

description: A rare but serious illness caused by a toxin that attacks the body's nerves.
causes: Ingesting contaminated food or through a wound infected with Clostridium botulinum.
symptoms: Facial weakness on both sides of the face
prevention: Proper food preservation and hygiene.
treatment_action: Antitoxin and supportive care (ventilator).
complications: Respiratory failure and long-term weakness.
medical_disclaimer: This information is for educational purposes only and is not a substitute for professional medical advice.

description: A mass or growth of abnormal cells in your brain.
causes: Genetic mutations and exposure to radiation.
symptoms: New onset or change in pattern of headaches
Gradual loss of sensation or movement in an arm or a leg
prevention: No known way to prevent brain tumors.
treatment_action: Surgery, radiation therapy, chemotherapy, and targeted drug therapy.
complications: Brain damage and permanent neurological deficits.
medical_disclaimer: This information is for educational purposes only and is not a substitute for professional medical advice.

description: A cancer that forms in the cells of the breasts.
causes: Genetics, hormonal factors, and lifestyle.
symptoms: Change in the size, shape or appearance of a breast
Changes to the skin over the breast
prevention: Regular screenings, maintaining a healthy weight, and limiting alcohol.
treatment_action: Surgery, radiation therapy, chemotherapy, and hormone therapy.
complications: Spread to other parts of the body.
medical_disclaimer: This information is for educational purposes only and is not a substitute for professional medical advice.

description: A condition where the lungs' airways become damaged, making it hard to clear mucus.
causes: Infections (like pneumonia or TB) or genetic conditions (like cystic fibrosis).
prevention: Prompt treatment of lung infections and getting vaccinated.
treatment_action: Antibiotics, chest physiotherapy, and oxygen therapy.
complications: Respiratory failure and heart failure.
medical_disclaimer: This information is for educational purposes only and is not a substitute for professional medical advice.

description: An infectious disease caused by bacteria that are spread from animals to people.
causes: Eating contaminated dairy products or direct contact with infected animals.
prevention: Avoid unpasteurized dairy and use caution when handling animals.
treatment_action: Antibiotics.
complications: Endocarditis, arthritis, and inflammation of the liver/spleen.
medical_disclaimer: This information is for educational purposes only and is not a substitute for professional medical advice.

description: A serious, potentially life-threatening eating disorder characterized by binge eating followed by purging.
causes: Genetics, biology, emotional health, and societal expectations.
symptoms: Preoccupation with body shape and weight
Living in fear of gaining weight
Repeated episodes of eating abnormally large amounts of food
Forcing yourself to vomit or exercising too much
prevention: Promoting a healthy body image and early intervention.
treatment_action: Psychotherapy and medications (antidepressants).
complications: Dehydration, heart problems, severe tooth decay, and digestive problems.
medical_disclaimer: This information is for educational purposes only and is not a substitute for professional medical advice.

description: A painful condition that affects the small, fluid-filled sacs — called bursae — that cushion the bones, tendons and muscles near your joints.
causes: Repetitive motions or positions that irritate the bursae.
symptoms: Pain when you move or press on the joint
prevention: Use cushions, take breaks, and maintain a healthy weight.
treatment_action: Rest, ice, and pain relievers. Physical therapy or injections may be needed.
complications: Chronic pain and loss of joint mobility.
medical_disclaimer: This information is for educational purposes only and is not a substitute for professional medical advice.

description: A rare, sometimes severe, disease caused by microscopic parasites that infect red blood cells.
causes: Spread by the bite of an infected tick.
prevention: Avoid tick-infested areas and use insect repellent.
treatment_action: Antiparasitic medications.
complications: Low blood pressure, liver problems, and kidney failure.
medical_disclaimer: This information is for educational purposes only and is not a substitute for professional medical advice.
